description: Hammer Blow: 60% energy, "50% increased accuracy", and it "guarantees 5 additional damage to that attack" — where the wiki is explicit that "even if the special attack misses, the target will still take a minimum of 5 damage from it". name: Ancient godsword
description: Blood Sacrifice: "doubled accuracy" and a "10% higher maximum hit than a normal attack" — the godsword multiplier again, so no per-weapon damage factor. The delayed sacrifice damage is deliberately NOT modelled, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. On a landed hit the target is marked, and eight ticks later takes 25 typeless damage unless it has moved five tiles away. Three things make it unmodelled here: whether the target escapes is a positional question this engine has no model for (the same reason chinchompa clumps are a player assertion); the damage is typeless, so it belongs to no part of the hit pipeline; and it lands eight ticks after the swing, which a steady-state per-attack model would have to amortise. The oracle omits it too, so no vector could validate an implementation either way. Against a stationary boss this understates the special by up to 25 damage per cast.

quotes: 10% higher maximum hit than a normal attack

That is a multi-target effect like the Hallowfell cleave and would read targetCount; the size-gated second hit is the single-target mechanic and the one this row covers.
